summary: Bitplane blending compositing (canonical name BitplaneBlendingCompositing): for each pair of adjacent source rows, blends the four 16-bit pixels seen through a sliding one-pixel window (two pixels from each row) into one 16-bit destination pixel per step, using 4-bit-per-channel masks 0xF0F0 and 0xF0F with rounding constants 8224 and 514. The source advances one row stride per outer iteration (adjacent-row pairs) and the destination advances its own row stride (this+0x1054), so this is a full-resolution compositing pass rather than a downscale. Always returns 0.

operations.description: Dereference this+0x0 to obtain the source surface object, then read its +0x18 field to get the source pixel-data base pointer.
Read the source row stride at obj+0x1050 and the blocks-per-row count at obj+0x105C, then compute the outer loop end bound as source base plus stride multiplied by blocks-per-row.
Read the destination surface object at this+0x4 and obtain its 16-bit pixel-data base pointer.

Outer row loop runs while the source pixel pointer is below the end bound; each pass processes the current source row against the next row (one stride ahead), advances the destination pointer by the destination row stride at this+0x1054, and advances the source by one source row stride.
Read the source block width at obj+0x1058 and form the inner loop row-end bound as the source pointer plus the width.

Inner loop slides a one-pixel window over each row pair, reading two 16-bit pixels from the current row and two from the next row (word offsets +0x0 and +0x2), writing one blended 16-bit pixel per step so the output row is one pixel narrower than the source row.

Blend the four pixels: average each 4-bit channel group separately, using mask 0xF0F0 with rounding constant 8224 and mask 0xF0F with rounding constant 514, shifting right by 2 and XOR-combining into the output pixel.
Return 0 after the outer loop completes; no error path exists.
